steps.body: $Q\to T$ and $T\to S\to P\to Q$: T reaches the cycle and is reached from it, so T joins.

steps.title: Absorb V
steps.body: $Q\to V$ and $V\to T\to S\to P\to Q$, so V joins as well.

steps.body: U has no outgoing edge, so it reaches nothing and forms its own SCC. Result: $\{P,Q,R,S,T,V\},\ \{U\}$.

At 6, P1 returns from I/O and preempts P2. P1 runs 6–8 (1 of 3 left). At 8, P3 returns and preempts P1; P3 runs 8–9 and **finishes at 9**.

steps.title: Interchange 2
steps.body: Consumer does Signal(F) before Signal(S). Signals never block; S is still released immediately after, so no process waits forever → **no deadlock**.

Reordering two signal operations cannot cause blocking.

Interchange 2 is harmless.

pitfalls: Treating reordered signals as dangerous; only waits can block.
it-2006-cs-55.verification: Scenario for 1: N items produced, producer enters with S, F = 0 → blocked; consumer Wait(E) succeeds, Wait(S) blocks → circular wait.
